name: Python Microservices
description: Full local stack for building and running Python microservices with Docker, Kubernetes, async task queues, caching, and a relational database.

notes.wsl: Windows Subsystem for Linux provides a real Linux environment. Required by Docker Desktop for its backend VM and gives access to native Linux tooling.
notes.docker: Industry-standard container runtime. Each microservice runs in its own container, ensuring consistent environments from dev to production.
notes.minikube: Runs a single-node Kubernetes cluster locally. Lets you test Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, and service meshes without a cloud account.
notes.kubectl: The official Kubernetes CLI. Used to deploy services, inspect pods, stream logs, and exec into containers in both local (minikube) and cloud clusters.
notes.helm: Kubernetes package manager. Helm charts package K8s manifests into versioned, configurable releases — used by nearly all production Kubernetes deployments.
notes.python: Primary language for the microservices. FastAPI + uvicorn is the dominant async Python web stack in 2024 for building high-performance APIs.
notes.nginx: High-performance reverse proxy and load balancer. Used as the API gateway in front of microservices, handling TLS termination and routing.
notes.mysql: Relational database for persistent data. MySQL 8.0 is widely adopted in microservices that require ACID transactions (orders, users, billing).
notes.git: Version control. Required by every workflow — source control, CI/CD triggers, Helm chart versioning, and team collaboration.
notes.node: Node.js runtime needed for frontend tooling (Vite, Next.js), as well as scripts and developer tools that ship as npm packages.
notes.postman: GUI tool for designing, testing, and documenting REST and GraphQL APIs. Supports environment variables for switching between local/staging/prod endpoints.
notes.dbeaver: Universal database GUI client. Connect to MySQL, inspect schema, run queries, and visualise data without writing CLI commands.
